name: Vampire Nocturnus
oracle_text:
Play with the top card of your library revealed.
As long as the top card of your library is black, this creature and other Vampire creatures you control get +2/+1 and have flying.
blocked_sentences: Play with the top card of your library revealed.
As long as the top card of your library is black, this creature and other Vampire creatures you control get +2/+1 and have flying.

needs.what: a continuous ability that keeps the top card of its controller's library face up and known to all players for as long as the source is on the battlefield, re-revealing automatically whenever the top card changes (draw, mill, shuffle, put_on_top, surveil, scry)
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `static_effects` has no revealing entry at all. `play_lands_from_library_top` is the only static that mentions the top of the library, but it grants a play permission and never exposes the card, so a card using it still cannot see what is on top. The `reveal` op is a one-shot on resolution -- it would show the card once as an enters-the-battlefield effect and never again, so the information would be stale the moment anything moved the library, and it is an effect rather than the continuous game-state change the printed line describes.

needs.what: a way to name the single card on top of a player's library and read its printed characteristics (here: whether it is black), usable inside an `if`/condition so a card can ask "the top card of your library is black"
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `selector_keys` has `zone` and `colors` but nothing positional -- no `top`, `from_top`, `index` or count-limited ordering key -- so the nearest expression, `exists` over `{zone: library, controller: you, colors: [B]}`, asks whether any black card is anywhere in the 40-card library. That is true almost always and is a different question from the printed one, which is why this cannot be approximated. `static_filter_keys` is narrower still and carries no `zone` key whatsoever, so a static ability's filter cannot reach outside the battlefield even if the positional key existed.
